chapterTitle: Born Again to a Living Hope
themeTitle: “You Shall Be Holy; for I Am Holy”

scripture.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen ones who are living as foreigners in the Dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
scripture.understanding: Πέτρος ἀπόστολος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, “Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ” — the name Jesus gave Simon, Πέτρος, ‘rock’ (John 1:42). ἀπόστολος, one sent with authority. ἐκλεκτοῖς παρεπιδήμοις διασπορᾶς, “to the chosen ones who are living as foreigners in the Dispersion” — ἐκλεκτός, chosen by God; παρεπίδημος, a resident alien, someone living temporarily in a land that is not his home; διασπορά, the scattering, the word James used (James 1:1). The five regions — Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia — cover most of northern and western Asia Minor, perhaps listed in the order a messenger would travel.

scripture.text: according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in sanctification of the Spirit, that you may obey Jesus Christ and be sprinkled with his blood: Grace to you and peace be multiplied.
scripture.understanding: κατὰ πρόγνωσιν θεοῦ πατρός, “according to the foreknowledge of God the Father” — πρόγνωσις, knowing beforehand, the loving choice of a Father, not mere information. ἐν ἁγιασμῷ πνεύματος, “in sanctification of the Spirit” — ἁγιασμός, being set apart as holy. εἰς ὑπακοὴν καὶ ῥαντισμὸν αἵματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, “that you may obey Jesus Christ and be sprinkled with his blood” — ὑπακοή, obedience, and ῥαντισμός, the sprinkling of covenant blood, as at Sinai (Exodus 24:7–8): the people promised to obey, and were sprinkled. Father, Spirit and Son work together in one sentence. πληθυνθείη, “be multiplied” — grace and peace growing more and more.

scripture.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
scripture.understanding: εὐλογητὸς ὁ θεός, “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ” — εὐλογητός, worthy of praise, a word used only of God. κατὰ τὸ πολὺ αὐτοῦ ἔλεος, “who according to his great mercy” — ἔλεος, from the mercy family: compassion that acts. ἀναγεννήσας ἡμᾶς, “caused us to be born again” — ἀναγεννάω, from the birth family: to beget again, Peter's word for what Jesus called being born ἄνωθεν (John 3:3). εἰς ἐλπίδα ζῶσαν, “to a living hope” — ζάω, from the life family: a hope that is alive because it rests on a living Lord, διὰ ἀναστάσεως, “through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead” — ἀνάστασις, from the rise family.

scripture.text: to an incorruptible and undefiled inheritance that doesn’t fade away, reserved in Heaven for you,
scripture.understanding: εἰς κληρονομίαν, “to an … inheritance” — κληρονομία, the allotted portion, as each tribe received its land in Canaan. Three negatives describe it: ἄφθαρτος, “incorruptible” — it cannot decay; ἀμίαντος, “undefiled” — it cannot be stained, the word James used for pure religion (James 1:27); ἀμάραντος, “that doesn’t fade away” — it cannot wither, unlike the rich man who ‘fades away’ (μαραίνω, James 1:11). τετηρημένην ἐν οὐρανοῖς, “reserved in Heaven for you” — τηρέω, from the hold family: kept under guard, already waiting with your name on it.

scripture.text: who by the power of God are guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
scripture.understanding: τοὺς ἐν δυνάμει θεοῦ φρουρουμένους, “who by the power of God are guarded” — δύναμις, from the power family: God's ability in action; φρουρέω, also from the hold family: a military word, to guard as a garrison guards a city. The inheritance is kept (τηρέω, v. 4); the heirs are guarded (φρουρέω). διὰ πίστεως, “through faith” — God's power works through your trust. εἰς σωτηρίαν ἑτοίμην ἀποκαλυφθῆναι ἐν καιρῷ ἐσχάτῳ, “for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time” — ἀποκαλύπτω, from the appear family: to unveil what already exists; καιρός, from the time family: the appointed moment, not χρόνος, a span of time.

scripture.text: Wherein you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been put to grief in various trials,
scripture.understanding: ἐν ᾧ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, “Wherein you greatly rejoice” — ἀγαλλιάω, exultant, leaping joy. ὀλίγον ἄρτι, “though now for a little while” — the same ‘little’ James used of the vapour of life (James 4:14). εἰ δέον, “if need be” — trials are never random; there is a ‘must’ in God's purpose. λυπηθέντες ἐν ποικίλοις πειρασμοῖς, “you have been put to grief in various trials” — λυπέω, to cause grief; ποικίλοι πειρασμοί, the exact words of James 1:2, ‘various temptations’: πειρασμός, from the test family, here as outward trials.

scripture.text: that the proof of your faith, which is more precious than gold that perishes even though it is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ—
scripture.understanding: ἵνα τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως, “that the proof of your faith” — δοκίμιον, from the test family, the same word as James 1:3, here the result of the assay: genuine faith. πολυτιμότερον χρυσίου τοῦ ἀπολλυμένου, “more precious than gold that perishes” — χρυσίον, gold. διὰ πυρὸς δὲ δοκιμαζομένου, “even though it is tested by fire” — δοκιμάζω, the verb of the test family. If perishable gold is worth refining, how much more imperishable faith. It will result in ἔπαινος, δόξα, τιμή — “praise, glory, and honor” — ἐν ἀποκαλύψει Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, “at the revelation of Jesus Christ” — ἀποκάλυψις, from the appear family: the unveiling of what is now hidden.

scripture.text: whom not having known you love; in whom, though now you don’t see him, yet believing, you rejoice greatly with joy unspeakable and full of glory—
scripture.understanding: ὃν οὐκ εἰδότες ἀγαπᾶτε, “whom not having known you love” — εἴδω, from the know family and the see family: the WEB follows manuscripts reading εἰδότες, ‘known’; most early manuscripts read ἰδόντες, ‘having seen’. Either way: unlike Peter, they never walked with Jesus in Galilee, yet they love Him — ἀγαπάω, from the love family. εἰς ὃν ἄρτι μὴ ὁρῶντες, “though now you don’t see him” — ὁράω, from the see family. πιστεύοντες δὲ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε χαρᾷ ἀνεκλαλήτῳ καὶ δεδοξασμένῃ, “yet believing, you rejoice greatly with joy unspeakable and full of glory” — ἀνεκλάλητος, beyond words; δοξάζω, glorified, joy already touched by heaven. Jesus called them blessed (John 20:29).

scripture.text: receiving the result of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
scripture.understanding: κομιζόμενοι τὸ τέλος τῆς πίστεως, “receiving the result of your faith” — κομίζω, to carry off as a prize; τέλος, from the perfect family: the end, the goal faith was always aiming at, as in James 5:11. σωτηρίαν ψυχῶν, “the salvation of your souls” — ψυχή, from the life family: your whole self, the life that outlasts the body.

scripture.text: Concerning this salvation, the prophets sought and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that would come to you,
scripture.understanding: περὶ ἧς σωτηρίας ἐξεζήτησαν καὶ ἐξηραύνησαν προφῆται, “Concerning this salvation, the prophets sought and searched diligently” — ἐκζητέω, to seek out; ἐξερευνάω, to search through, as a miner searches for ore. οἱ περὶ τῆς εἰς ὑμᾶς χάριτος προφητεύσαντες, “who prophesied of the grace that would come to you” — the Old Testament prophets spoke of a grace they themselves would not see.

scripture.text: searching for who or what kind of time the Spirit of Christ, which was in them, pointed to, when he predicted the sufferings of Christ, and the glories that would follow them.
scripture.understanding: ἐρευνῶντες εἰς τίνα ἢ ποῖον καιρόν, “searching for who or what kind of time” — καιρός, from the time family: the appointed season, as in verse 5. τὸ ἐν αὐτοῖς πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ, “the Spirit of Christ, which was in them” — the Spirit who inspired the prophets is the Spirit of Christ, a striking witness to Christ's pre-existence. προμαρτυρόμενον τὰ εἰς Χριστὸν παθήματα καὶ τὰς μετὰ ταῦτα δόξας, “when he predicted the sufferings of Christ, and the glories that would follow them” — πάθημα, from the suffer family: what one undergoes; δόξα, glory. The theme of the whole letter in one line: sufferings, then glories.

scripture.text: To them it was revealed, that not to themselves, but to you, they ministered these things, which now have been announced to you through those who preached the Good News to you by the Holy Spirit sent out from heaven; which things angels desire to look into.
scripture.understanding: οἷς ἀπεκαλύφθη, “To them it was revealed” — ἀποκαλύπτω, from the appear family. ὅτι οὐχ ἑαυτοῖς ὑμῖν δὲ διηκόνουν αὐτά, “that not to themselves, but to you, they ministered these things” — διακονέω, from the servant family: the prophets were servants, waiting tables for a feast they would not eat. ἀνηγγέλη, “announced,” εὐαγγελισαμένων, “preached the Good News.” εἰς ἃ ἐπιθυμοῦσιν ἄγγελοι παρακύψαι, “which things angels desire to look into” — παρακύπτω, from the see family: to stoop and peer in, the word used of the disciples looking into the empty tomb and of the one who ‘looks into’ the perfect law (James 1:25). Even angels bend down to look at the gospel.

scripture.text: Therefore prepare your minds for action, be sober, and set your hope fully on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ—
scripture.understanding: διὸ ἀναζωσάμενοι τὰς ὀσφύας τῆς διανοίας ὑμῶν, “Therefore prepare your minds for action” — literally ‘gird up the loins of your mind’: tuck your long robe into your belt so you can run, as Israel ate the Passover dressed for travel (Exodus 12:11). διάνοια, the thinking mind. νήφοντες, “be sober” — νήφω, from the self-control family: clear-headed, not intoxicated by anything. τελείως ἐλπίσατε, “set your hope fully” — τελείως, from the perfect family: completely, without holding anything back. ἐπὶ τὴν φερομένην ὑμῖν χάριν ἐν ἀποκαλύψει Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, “on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ” — ἀποκάλυψις, from the appear family, as in verse 7.

scripture.text: as children of obedience, not conforming yourselves according to your former lusts as in your ignorance,
scripture.understanding: ὡς τέκνα ὑπακοῆς, “as children of obedience” — a Hebrew way of saying ‘obedient children’, children whose family likeness is obedience. μὴ συσχηματιζόμενοι, “not conforming yourselves” — συσχηματίζω, from the image family: to shape yourself to an outward mould (σχῆμα), the word Paul uses in Romans 12:2. ταῖς πρότερον ἐν τῇ ἀγνοίᾳ ὑμῶν ἐπιθυμίαις, “according to your former lusts as in your ignorance” — ἐπιθυμία, desire; ἄγνοια, the ignorance of people who did not yet know God, a sign that many readers were Gentiles. τέκνον is from the children family — a child — one born of a parent, family by birth.

scripture.text: but just as he who called you is holy, you yourselves also be holy in all of your behavior;
scripture.understanding: ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸν καλέσαντα ὑμᾶς ἅγιον, “but just as he who called you is holy” — καλέω, to call, God's effective summons. ἅγιος, holy: set apart, different, belonging wholly to God. καὶ αὐτοὶ ἅγιοι ἐν πάσῃ ἀναστροφῇ γενήθητε, “you yourselves also be holy in all of your behavior” — ἀναστροφή, way of life, the same word James used for ‘good conduct’ (James 3:13). Holiness is not one compartment of life; it is ‘all’.

scripture.text: because it is written, “You shall be holy; for I am holy.”
scripture.understanding: διότι γέγραπται, “because it is written, ‘You shall be holy; for I am holy.’” — from Leviticus 11:44–45 and 19:2. ἅγιος twice. The command rests on God's character: His people are to resemble Him. The holiness code once separated Israel from the nations by food and ritual; now it separates the church from the world by a holy life.

scripture.text: If you call on him as Father, who without respect of persons judges according to each man’s work, pass the time of your living as foreigners here in reverent fear:
scripture.understanding: καὶ εἰ πατέρα ἐπικαλεῖσθε, “If you call on him as Father” — ἐπικαλέομαι, to call upon in prayer. τὸν ἀπροσωπολήμπτως κρίνοντα, “who without respect of persons judges” — ἀπροσωπολήπτως, without ‘receiving faces’, the opposite of the favouritism James condemned (James 2:1). κατὰ τὸ ἑκάστου ἔργον, “according to each man’s work” — ἔργον, from the work family: the whole of a life's work, singular. ἐν φόβῳ τὸν τῆς παροικίας ὑμῶν χρόνον ἀναστράφητε, “pass the time of your living as foreigners here in reverent fear” — χρόνος, from the time family: the span of your stay, not καιρός, the appointed moment of verses 5 and 11; παροικία, temporary residence. Your Father is also the Judge, and your time here is short.

scripture.text: knowing that you were redeemed, not with corruptible things, with silver or gold, from the useless way of life handed down from your fathers,
scripture.understanding: εἰδότες ὅτι οὐ φθαρτοῖς, ἀργυρίῳ ἢ χρυσίῳ, ἐλυτρώθητε, “knowing that you were redeemed, not with corruptible things, with silver or gold” — εἰδότες, from εἴδω, of the know family (and the see family): knowing as settled fact. λυτρόω, from the redeem family: to set free by paying a ransom, the price paid for a slave or captive. φθαρτός, perishable, the opposite of the ‘incorruptible’ inheritance (v. 4). ἐκ τῆς ματαίας ὑμῶν ἀναστροφῆς πατροπαραδότου, “from the useless way of life handed down from your fathers” — μάταιος, empty, the word James used for worthless religion (James 1:26). Tradition is not freedom; Christ is.

scripture.text: but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish or spot, the blood of Christ;
scripture.understanding: ἀλλὰ τιμίῳ αἵματι, “but with precious blood” — τίμιος, of great value, honoured. ὡς ἀμνοῦ ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου Χριστοῦ, “as of a lamb without blemish or spot, the blood of Christ” — ἀμνός, a lamb, the Passover lamb that had to be perfect (Exodus 12:5), and the Lamb John the Baptist pointed to (John 1:29). ἄμωμος, without inner defect; ἄσπιλος, without outward spot, the word James used for being ‘unstained by the world’ (James 1:27). ἀμνός is from the lamb family — a lamb, especially the sacrificial lamb.

scripture.text: who was foreknown indeed before the foundation of the world, but was revealed in this last age for your sake,
scripture.understanding: προεγνωσμένου μὲν πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, “who was foreknown indeed before the foundation of the world” — προγινώσκω, to know beforehand, as in verse 2; καταβολή, laying down a foundation; κόσμος, from the world family: the ordered creation. The cross was not God's emergency plan. φανερωθέντος δὲ ἐπ᾽ ἐσχάτου τῶν χρόνων, “but was revealed in this last age for your sake” — φανερόω, from the appear family: to make visible, to bring into the open, as distinct from ἀποκαλύπτω (to unveil, vv. 5, 12). χρόνος, from the time family, here rendered ‘age’: the last span of time before the end.

scripture.text: who through him are believers in God, who raised him from the dead, and gave him glory; so that your faith and hope might be in God.
scripture.understanding: τοὺς δι᾽ αὐτοῦ πιστοὺς εἰς θεόν, “who through him are believers in God” — πιστός, faithful, believing. τὸν ἐγείραντα αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ δόξαν αὐτῷ δόντα, “who raised him from the dead, and gave him glory” — ἐγείρω, from the rise family: to raise up. Sufferings, then glory (v. 11). ὥστε τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν καὶ ἐλπίδα εἶναι εἰς θεόν, “so that your faith and hope might be in God” — faith rests on what God has done; hope rests on what He will do.

scripture.text: Seeing you have purified your souls in your obedience to the truth through the Spirit in sincere brotherly affection, love one another from the heart fervently:
scripture.understanding: τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν ἡγνικότες, “Seeing you have purified your souls” — ψυχή, from the life family: the whole inner self; ἁγνίζω, to make clean, the word James used: ‘purify your hearts’ (James 4:8). ἐν τῇ ὑπακοῇ τῆς ἀληθείας, “in your obedience to the truth” — conversion is obedience to the gospel. εἰς φιλαδελφίαν ἀνυπόκριτον, “in sincere brotherly affection” — φιλαδελφία, from the love family: the warm family affection of brothers and sisters; ἀνυπόκριτος, unfeigned. ἐκ καρδίας ἀλλήλους ἀγαπήσατε ἐκτενῶς, “love one another from the heart fervently” — ἀγαπάω, also from the love family: the committed, self-giving love of the will. Peter puts the two side by side: you already have φιλαδελφία; now stretch it into ἀγάπη. ἐκτενῶς, ‘stretched out’, like a runner straining for the line.

scripture.text: having been born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, through the word of God, which lives and remains forever.
scripture.understanding: ἀναγεγεννημένοι, “having been born again” — ἀναγεννάω, from the birth family, as in verse 3. οὐκ ἐκ σπορᾶς φθαρτῆς ἀλλὰ ἀφθάρτου, “not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible” — σπορά, seed, sowing. διὰ λόγου ζῶντος θεοῦ καὶ μένοντος, “through the word of God, which lives and remains forever” — λόγος, from the word family: the whole message God has spoken; ζάω, from the life family. The new life is as permanent as the seed it grows from. James said the same: God ‘gave birth to us by the word of truth’ (James 1:18).

scripture.text: For, “All flesh is like grass, and all of man’s glory like the flower in the grass. The grass withers, and its flower falls;
scripture.understanding: “For, ‘All flesh is like grass, and all of man’s glory like the flower in the grass.’” — from Isaiah 40:6–8, the passage James also echoed (James 1:10–11). σάρξ, human life in its frailty; χόρτος, grass; ἄνθος, flower. ἐξηράνθη ὁ χόρτος καὶ τὸ ἄνθος ἐξέπεσεν, “The grass withers, and its flower falls” — ξηραίνω, to dry up; ἐκπίπτω, to fall off.

scripture.text: but the Lord’s word endures forever.” This is the word of Good News which was preached to you.
scripture.understanding: τὸ δὲ ῥῆμα κυρίου μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, “but the Lord’s word endures forever” — ῥῆμα, from the word family: the spoken word, a particular utterance, as distinct from λόγος in verse 23, the whole message. Peter uses both. αἰών, in both the time family and the world family: the age, unending, as distinct from κόσμος, the ordered world. τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν τὸ ῥῆμα τὸ εὐαγγελισθὲν εἰς ὑμᾶς, “This is the word of Good News which was preached to you” — the eternal word of Isaiah is the very gospel these exiles heard.

visualMeditations.title: The Inheritance in the Vault
visualMeditations.image: Picture a great vault deep inside a fortress. Inside, on a table, lies a sealed document with your name on it — the title to an inheritance. Moths cannot reach it, rust cannot touch it, thieves cannot break in. Outside the vault, soldiers stand guard. And on the road towards the fortress, you yourself are walking, surrounded by a second company of soldiers who guard you every step of the journey home.
visualMeditations.meaning: “to an incorruptible and undefiled inheritance that doesn’t fade away, reserved in Heaven for you” (v. 4), “who by the power of God are guarded through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time” (v. 5). God guards both ends: the inheritance is kept for you, and you are kept for the inheritance. Your living hope does not depend on how strong you feel today, but on the power of God that guards you.

visualMeditations.title: Gold in the Furnace
visualMeditations.image: Picture a goldsmith's furnace glowing white-hot. He drops a lump of ore into the crucible. It melts, bubbles, and impurities rise to the surface. He skims them off, again and again, until the gold is pure. Then he holds it up to the light — and it gleams. Yet even that refined gold will one day be lost or melted down. What Peter describes is more precious still.
visualMeditations.meaning: “that the proof of your faith, which is more precious than gold that perishes even though it is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ” (v. 7). If people put gold through fire to prove it, God will put faith through fire to prove it — and faith, unlike gold, lasts forever. Your trial is ‘for a little while’ (v. 6); its result is eternal.

visualMeditations.title: Angels Bending Down
visualMeditations.image: Picture the prophets of old bent over their scrolls by lamplight, searching their own words for clues — when will Messiah come? Who will He be? What will His sufferings mean? Then picture the angels of heaven leaning over the edge of eternity, stooping to look into what God has done for human beings, longing to understand it.
visualMeditations.meaning: “Concerning this salvation, the prophets sought and searched diligently, who prophesied of the grace that would come to you” (v. 10). Their message was “not to themselves, but to you” (v. 12), and it contains “things angels desire to look into” (v. 12). You hold in your hands what prophets longed to see and angels long to understand. Never treat the gospel as ordinary.

visualMeditations.title: The Spotless Lamb
visualMeditations.image: Picture a slave market in a Roman city. A man stands in chains, waiting to be sold. A stranger steps forward and pays the price — not with a bag of silver, but by giving his own life. The chains fall off. Then picture an Israelite family on Passover night, choosing a perfect, unblemished lamb, and painting its blood on their doorposts.
visualMeditations.meaning: “knowing that you were redeemed, not with corruptible things, with silver or gold, from the useless way of life handed down from your fathers” (v. 18), “but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish or spot, the blood of Christ” (v. 19). You were bought out of an empty, inherited way of life by the most precious price in the universe. That is why you can live differently.

structure.label: Greeting (v. 1-2)
structure.body: Peter, an apostle, writes to the chosen exiles scattered through Asia Minor, chosen by the Father, set apart by the Spirit, for obedience to Jesus Christ and sprinkling with His blood.

structure.label: A Living Hope (v. 3-9)
structure.body: Praise God, who gave new birth to a living hope through the resurrection, to an imperishable inheritance kept in heaven for those guarded by His power; though grieved by trials for a little while, their tested faith will bring praise and glory when Christ is revealed; they love and trust Him without seeing Him, receiving the salvation of their souls.

structure.label: The Prophets and the Angels (v. 10-12)
structure.body: The prophets searched for the time of Christ's sufferings and glories, serving not themselves but us; angels long to look into the gospel now preached by the Spirit.

structure.label: Be Holy (v. 13-21)
structure.body: With minds prepared and sober, set your hope fully on the coming grace; as obedient children, do not conform to former desires but be holy in all conduct, because God is holy; live in reverent fear, knowing you were redeemed not with silver or gold but with the precious blood of Christ, the spotless Lamb foreknown before creation.

structure.label: Love from a Pure Heart (v. 22-25)
structure.body: Having purified yourselves by obeying the truth, love one another earnestly, for you have been born again of imperishable seed through the living and enduring word of God, the gospel preached to you.

sections.heading: A Living Hope for People Without a Home
paragraphs: Peter begins by telling his readers who they are. They are ‘foreigners’ and ‘scattered’ — words that describe their social situation. But they are also “chosen ones” (v. 1), chosen by the Father, set apart by the Spirit, sprinkled with the blood of Jesus (v. 2). Their identity is not defined by their neighbours' opinion but by the work of the Trinity. Before Peter gives a single command, he establishes their security.

Then he bursts into praise: “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead” (v. 3). Every word matters. New birth is God's mercy, not human achievement. The hope is ‘living’ because it rests on a risen Saviour. Peter knew what a dead hope felt like: after the crucifixion, he and the other disciples had hidden behind locked doors. The resurrection made their hope alive again — and Peter never forgot it.

This hope looks forward to an inheritance that cannot decay, be stained or fade (v. 4). Everything in this world does all three. But Peter adds something even more comforting: believers themselves are “guarded through faith” by the power of God (v. 5). The inheritance is kept for you, and you are kept for it. Paul says the same: “And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus” (Philippians 4:7) — using the same military word.

sections.heading: Joy and Grief Together
paragraphs: Peter is honest: believers both rejoice and grieve. “Wherein you greatly rejoice, though now for a little while, if need be, you have been put to grief in various trials” (v. 6). Joy does not cancel grief, and grief does not cancel joy. Both are real at the same time. The phrase ‘if need be’ is important: trials are not random. God permits them for a purpose.

That purpose is the proving of faith (v. 7). Peter uses the same words as James — ‘various trials’ (James 1:2) and ‘the testing of your faith’ (James 1:3) — and adds the picture of gold in the furnace. The goal is not destruction but revelation: “praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ” (v. 7). On that day, the faith that held on in the fire will be honoured by the One it trusted.

Then Peter says something deeply personal: “whom not having known you love; in whom, though now you don’t see him, yet believing, you rejoice greatly with joy unspeakable and full of glory” (v. 8). Peter had seen Jesus — walked with Him, eaten with Him, denied Him and been restored by Him. His readers had never seen Him. Yet they loved Him just as truly. Jesus had told Thomas, “Blessed are those who have not seen, and have believed” (John 20:29). That blessing belongs to every believer who reads this letter.

sections.heading: Holy Because He Is Holy
paragraphs: With verse 13 the letter turns from what God has done to how believers should live. The first command is about the mind: “Therefore prepare your minds for action, be sober, and set your hope fully on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ” (v. 13). Before you can live differently, you must think differently — alert, clear-headed and fixed on the future grace.

The second command is holiness: “but just as he who called you is holy, you yourselves also be holy in all of your behavior” (v. 15). This is not a new idea; it comes from Leviticus. But it has a new setting. Once, Israel was set apart from the nations by food laws and rituals. Now, the church is set apart by its whole way of life. Peter's readers had been shaped by “your former lusts as in your ignorance” (v. 14). Now they are to be shaped by the character of the God who called them. Hebrews says the same: “Follow after peace with all men, and the sanctification without which no man will see the Lord” (Hebrews 12:14).

The motive for holiness is the cost of redemption. “knowing that you were redeemed, not with corruptible things, with silver or gold” (v. 18), “but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish or spot, the blood of Christ” (v. 19). Peter had once tried to stop Jesus going to the cross (Matthew 16:22). Now he understands that the cross was planned “before the foundation of the world” (v. 20). The price was infinite, so the purchase is precious. You cannot treat lightly a life that cost the blood of God's Son.

sections.heading: Born of an Imperishable Word
paragraphs: The chapter ends with love and the word. “Seeing you have purified your souls in your obedience to the truth through the Spirit in sincere brotherly affection, love one another from the heart fervently” (v. 22). Peter uses two love words: φιλαδελφία, the warm affection of family, which they already have, and ἀγάπη, the committed love of the will, which must be stretched to its full length. Church family affection must grow into fervent, sacrificial love.

The reason is their new birth: “having been born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, through the word of God, which lives and remains forever” (v. 23). Peter quotes Isaiah to show the contrast between human frailty and God's permanence: “For, ‘All flesh is like grass, and all of man’s glory like the flower in the grass. The grass withers, and its flower falls’” (v. 24), “but the Lord’s word endures forever” (v. 25). Everything human fades; God's word does not. And that eternal word is not far away: “This is the word of Good News which was preached to you” (v. 25).

ntConnection.heading: New Birth, the Lamb and the Seeking Prophets
paragraphs: Peter's teaching on new birth echoes Jesus' words to Nicodemus: “Most certainly, I tell you, unless one is born anew, he can’t see God’s Kingdom” (John 3:3). James uses a different verb for the same truth: “Of his own will he gave birth to us by the word of truth” (James 1:18). Both James and Peter tie new birth to God's word — the seed that produces life.

The spotless Lamb of verse 19 is the Lamb John the Baptist announced: “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” (John 1:29). Hebrews explains what His blood achieved: “nor yet through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, entered in once for all into the Holy Place, having obtained eternal redemption” (Hebrews 9:12). And in heaven the redeemed sing: “for you were killed, and bought us for God with your blood, out of every tribe, language, people, and nation” (Revelation 5:9). Peter's ‘precious blood’ is heaven's eternal song.

The searching prophets of verses 10–12 recall the risen Jesus on the road to Emmaus: “Didn’t the Christ have to suffer these things and to enter into his glory?” (Luke 24:26). “Beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, he explained to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself” (Luke 24:27). Peter heard Jesus explain the same things after the resurrection (Acts 1:3). The sufferings and the glories that the prophets glimpsed are the heart of the gospel Peter now preaches — and the pattern his readers must follow.

lexicon.insight: Strong's: “to beget or (by extension) bear (again).” ἀναγεννάω appears only twice in the New Testament, both times in this chapter. It describes what Jesus told Nicodemus, using γεννάω with ἄνωθεν: a birth from above, a second beginning. Peter emphasises the cause (God's great mercy, v. 3), the means (the living word, v. 23) and the result (a living hope and an imperishable inheritance). This study gathers these words into a new birth family. New birth is not a religious upgrade; it is a new life from a new Father.

Strong's: “to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect.” φρουρέω is a military word: a garrison guarding a city. Paul uses it of the peace of God that guards hearts (Philippians 4:7). Peter pairs it with τηρέω in verse 4 — both from the hold family. The inheritance is kept; the heirs are guarded. You are not holding on to God by your own strength; His power is holding you.

Strong's: “an alien alongside, i.e. a resident foreigner.” παρεπίδημος describes someone living away from home, a sojourner. Peter uses it with παροικία (v. 17), a temporary stay in a place that is not your country. Abraham called himself a stranger and sojourner among the Hittites (Genesis 23:4), and Hebrews says the heroes of faith confessed they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth. Christians are not citizens who happen to be religious; they are citizens of heaven living for a time abroad.

Strong's: “to ransom (literally or figuratively).” λυτρόω comes from λύτρον, the ransom price paid to free a slave or prisoner. Jesus said the Son of Man came “to give his life as a ransom for many” (Matthew 20:28). Peter stresses the price: not silver or gold, which perish, but precious blood. This study adds a new redeem family, with the market words ἀγοράζω and ἐξαγοράζω. Redemption is not merely forgiveness; it is a change of ownership.

Strong's: “an utterance (individually, collectively or specially).” Peter uses both members of the word family within three verses. In verse 23 it is λόγος — the word of God as a whole message, the seed of new life. In verse 25, quoting Isaiah, it is ῥῆμα — the word spoken, a particular utterance. And he identifies that ῥῆμα with the gospel preached to them. The message as a whole and every spoken promise within it share the same quality: they live and remain forever.

holySpiritRevelation.intro: In this chapter the Holy Spirit is lifting your eyes from your circumstances to your inheritance — and calling you to live a holy life that matches your new birth.

items.title: Your Hope Is Alive
items.body: Is your hope tired, fading or almost dead? The Spirit reminds you that your hope is living because Jesus is alive. “who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead” (v. 3). Whatever has died in your life — a dream, a relationship, a plan — your hope in Christ has not. Ask Him to breathe life into your hope again today.

items.title: You Are Being Guarded
items.body: You may feel that you are barely holding on. The Spirit wants you to know that God is holding you. You are “guarded through faith” by the power of God (v. 5). Your trial is ‘for a little while’; your inheritance is forever. Where have you been trusting your own strength to keep going? Rest in His.

items.title: Holy in All Your Conduct
items.body: The Spirit is gently pointing to an area where you are still being shaped by “your former lusts” (v. 14) instead of by God's holiness. It may be a habit, a pattern of speech, a way of spending money, or an inherited way of life from your family or culture. “you yourselves also be holy in all of your behavior” (v. 15). You were bought with precious blood. What does He want you to lay down?

audit.title: The Hope Check
audit.body: Where is your hope set — on your plans, your finances, your relationships, or “fully on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ” (v. 13)? What would change if your hope were fully fixed on His coming?

audit.title: The Conformity Check
audit.body: In what areas are you still “conforming yourselves according to your former lusts” (v. 14)? What ‘useless way of life handed down from your fathers’ (v. 18) still shapes you?

audit.title: The Love Check
audit.body: Is your love for other believers sincere and fervent (v. 22)? Who in your church family do you find hard to love from the heart? What would ‘stretched out’ love look like towards them?

practices.title: Write Your Inheritance Statement
practices.body: Tonight, write at the top of a page: ‘My inheritance — incorruptible, undefiled, unfading, kept in heaven for me.’ Below it, list the things in your life that are perishing (possessions, health, status, plans) and, opposite them, the things God has promised that cannot perish. Read verses 3–9 aloud over the list and thank God for each promise. Keep it in your Bible for days of trial.

practices.title: A Week of Holy Conduct
practices.body: Choose one area of your conduct — speech, entertainment, money, work, relationships — and for one week ask before every decision in that area: ‘Is this holy, as He who called me is holy?’ (v. 15). Write down one change you made each day. At the end of the week, thank Christ for the precious blood that bought you, and ask Him to make the change permanent.

prayerReflection: “Blessed be You, God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. According to Your great mercy You caused me to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus from the dead. Thank You for an inheritance that is incorruptible, undefiled and unfading, kept in heaven for me, and thank You that by Your power I am guarded through faith until the salvation that is ready to be revealed. When I am grieved by various trials for a little while, let my faith be proved like gold in the fire and found to bring praise and glory to Jesus at His revelation. I have not seen Him, yet I love Him; I do not see Him now, yet I believe and rejoice with joy beyond words. Prepare my mind for action, make me sober, and help me set my hope fully on the grace that is coming. You are holy, Lord, so make me holy in all my conduct. Thank You that I was redeemed not with silver or gold but with the precious blood of Christ, the spotless Lamb. Let me love my brothers and sisters fervently from a pure heart, because I have been born again of the imperishable seed of Your living and enduring word. In Jesus' name, Amen.”

storyConnections.title: Peter's Dead Hope Comes Alive
storyConnections.summary: After the crucifixion Peter's hope was dead. He had denied Jesus three times and wept bitterly; now his Lord was in a tomb. On the first day of the week the women brought word that the tomb was empty. Peter ran to it, stooped down and saw the linen cloths lying by themselves, and went home wondering. That evening the disciples were saying, “The Lord is risen indeed, and has appeared to Simon!” (Luke 24:34). When Peter later writes that God has caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection, he is writing about the day his own hope came back to life.

storyConnections.title: The Passover Lamb
storyConnections.summary: On the night God brought Israel out of Egypt, each household was to take a lamb ‘without blemish, a male a year old’, keep it for four days, then kill it at twilight and put its blood on the doorposts. That night the Lord passed through Egypt in judgement, but when He saw the blood He passed over the house. The people ate the meal dressed for travel, with their belts fastened and their sandals on — ready to leave slavery behind. Peter's words echo the whole scene: redeemed by the blood of a lamb without blemish (v. 19), minds girded for action (v. 13), and called out of an old way of life as pilgrims (vv. 1, 17).

storyConnections.title: Peter Restored to Feed the Sheep
storyConnections.summary: By the Sea of Galilee the risen Jesus asked Peter three times whether he loved Him. The first two times He used ἀγαπάω, and Peter answered with φιλέω, ‘you know that I have affection for you’; the third time Jesus used Peter's own word. Each time He gave a command: “Feed my lambs” (John 21:15), “Tend my sheep” (John 21:16), “Feed my sheep” (John 21:17). First Peter is that command being obeyed. The man who was asked about love now tells the flock, “love one another from the heart fervently” (v. 22) — and speaks of a Christ whom they love though they have not seen Him.
